title.narrative: Supporting the shift towards Integrated, Low-Carbon and Nature-Positive Neighborhoods in Nairobi

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Supporting integrated, low-carbon, and nature-positive urban development in Kenya through the adoption of policies, capacity building, neighborhood design, pilot implementation and resource mobilization, to generate global environmental benefits.

The Nairobi Sustainable City Integrated Project is poised to deliver substantial socio-economic benefits by fostering inclusive urban transformation, improving service delivery, and enhancing resilience for vulnerable communities. By embedding nature-positive and low-carbon approaches into neighborhood planning and infrastructure development, the project will contribute to a higher quality of life, better access to green public spaces, and more equitable access to basic services such as mobility, energy, and sanitation. A core benefit will be job creation, particularly for youth and women, through investments in green construction, infrastructure maintenance, urban agriculture, and waste management. For instance, the development and maintenance of sustainable transport systems, riparian corridors, waste management projects, climate-resilient innovations are expected to generate both short-term employment during construction and longer-term green jobs across sectors. The project will also contribute to public health and economic savings by reducing exposure to air and water pollution, enhancing access to non-motorized transport options, and improving drainage and sanitation systems. These improvements are expected to lower the incidence of respiratory and waterborne diseases, reducing pressure on the public health system and enabling greater economic productivity. Furthermore, energy-efficient housing and transport infrastructure will result in household cost savings and reduced dependence on fossil fuels, enhancing overall economic resilience. Finally, by reducing vulnerabilities to climate risks—such as urban flooding, heat stress, and service disruptions—the project will help avoid future economic losses and improve the adaptive capacity of Nairobi’s growing population. In doing so, it supports a just and inclusive green transition that places communities, particularly those in informal settlements, at the heart of the city’s development trajectory.
